title: The Galaxy-Cluster Residual in de Sitter-MOND: the Dark Sector Has the Mass, but a Density-Ordering Veto Forbids It from Being Galaxy-Safe and Cluster-Clumpy at Once
description: MOND and its relativistic completions reproduce galaxy rotation curves with one acceleration scale a0 but leave a factor-~2 missing-mass residual in galaxy-cluster cores (Sanders 1999, 2003), shared across the whole relativistic-MOND family. We ask whether this residual is explained WITHIN the de Sitter-MOND framework (a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = cH_Lambda/Z, Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.7888, a0 = 9.36e-11 m/s^2), whose dark sector is the Aether-Scalar-Tensor (AeST) ghost-condensate of Skordis & Zlosnik (2021): a cold, w=0, rho~a^-3 MODE of the gravity field, not a new particle. We report a clean two-sided result. (i) The abundance is NOT the problem: the AeST shift-symmetric Q-mode carries Omega_dm worth of cold density, which at the cosmic dark-to-baryon ratio supplies ~7.0e14 Msun inside R500 against the ~4.79e14 a factor-2 cluster requires -- a ratio of 1.46, with ZERO mass tuning. The framework's dark sector HAS the cluster mass. (ii) But it cannot deploy that mass galaxy-safely: the Q-mode is sound-speed-zero (c_s^2 -> 0) sub-horizon -- the very property that lets AeST fit the Planck third acoustic peak -- so its Jeans length vanishes and growth is gated only by the mass term rho > mu^2/4piG. Galaxy disks and cluster cores both exceed this by ~10^13, AND the galaxy disk is ~3.7x DENSER than the cluster core: the density ordering runs BACKWARDS, so any field that clumps in cluster cores clumps MORE in galaxies. Injecting the required density into a fiducial disk shifts the radial-acceleration relation by +0.12 to +0.23 dex against a 0.11-0.14 dex scatter floor -- re-introducing the cuspy-halo scatter MOND was built to remove. No acceleration gate evades this: a0 is absent from the AeST linear perturbations (Bridge-1), so the dust grows CDM-identically. The conclusion is a no-go, stated symmetrically: the residual IS the framework's own dark sector doing a cold-dark-matter job -- that is the explanation -- but in the two clean field limits the sector either over-fills clusters and breaks galaxies, or stays galaxy-safe and fills only ~17-20% of the core. There is no limit in which it does both. The 'pure MOND, no dark matter' reading is forfeited: the framework contains dark matter, of a non-particle (gravity-mode) kind. A galaxy-safe no-new-particle stack (the Y-Q response +17-20%, intracluster-light/baryons within the cosmic baryon ceiling, budget-capped stellar remnants) closes ~36% of the robust ~1e14 Msun core gap, leaving ~64% open; the core gap is robust (resolved core weak-lensing/X-ray ratio ~1.03, so it is not deflated by the weak-lensing-vs-hydrostatic question). The one open theory lever to close it galaxy-safely is the AeST mass scale mu^-1 threading an intermediate regime between galaxy and cluster scales -- currently uncomputed, pinnable by a joint CMB+galaxy-weak-lensing fit. Two negative results close common escapes: the framework's history-dependent modified inertia is WRONG-SIGNED for a surplus (d ln M_eff / d ln a0 = -1 exactly), and the neutrino (hot-dark-matter) option is excluded by KATRIN (2024) and DESI DR2 (2025). All quantitative claims are reproduced by committed Python scripts (all exit 0) at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula. Quarantine note: a0, Z, kappa, and the dark-sector amplitude I0 are inputs/free parameters, never asserted to be derived. This is a both-sided consistency analysis of an existing theory's dark sector, not a discovery paper and not a claim of a theory of everything.
